assumptions: Records from one file are one genome, scored against that genome's pooled codon usage.
The genetic code given is the one the genes are translated with.
limits: An outlier is typically highly expressed or of unusual composition; it is not evidence of horizontal transfer.
Genes below the minimum codon count are left out and listed.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which genes of a genome use synonymous codons in a way the genome's own average does not explain?

description: Score every coding sequence of a genome against the genome's own codon usage and report the genes whose synonymous codon choice that average does not explain, with the false discovery rate controlled across the genes. Records from different files are different genomes: each is scored against its own file's usage, and the false discovery rate is controlled once across every gene of every genome. Each gene gets Karlin's B and Supek & Vlahoviček's MILC against the pooled usage of the genes, and a G-test of its codon choice within each amino acid against that usage (χ², degrees of freedom from the amino acids it uses). Outliers are typically highly expressed genes (ribosomal proteins are the most deviant class), genes of unusual composition, and some of foreign origin; an outlier is NOT evidence of horizontal transfer, since codon bias is a poor indicator of transfer.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alpha.description: false discovery rate at which a gene is reported as an outlier.

alt_init.description: count every alternative start codon as Met throughout each gene, as coRdon does by default. Off reads an internal alternative start codon as its own amino acid. Advanced.

correction.description: Benjamini–Hochberg (independent or positively dependent tests) or Benjamini–Yekutieli (any dependence; less power). Values: BH (Benjamini–Hochberg), BY (Benjamini–Yekutieli).

file_codes.description: a genetic code for one file, as `file=code` (e.g. `Mycoplasma_genitalium_cds.fna=4`): that file's genes are read with it, every other file with genetic_code. For a corpus whose genomes translate differently. Advanced.

genetic_code.description: NCBI genetic code the genes are read with (4 for Mycoplasma, 11 for most bacteria; 1 and 11 group codons identically). Values: 1 (1 · Standard), 2 (2 · Vertebrate Mitochondrial), 3 (3 · Yeast Mitochondrial), 4 (4 · Mold Mitochondrial, Protozoan Mitochondrial, Coelenterate Mitochondrial, Mycoplasma, Spiroplasma), 5 (5 · Invertebrate Mitochondrial), 6 (6 · Ciliate Nuclear, Dasycladacean Nuclear, Hexamita Nuclear), 9 (9 · Echinoderm Mitochondrial, Flatworm Mitochondrial), 10 (10 · Euplotid Nuclear), 11 (11 · Bacterial, Archaeal and Plant Plastid), 12 (12 · Alternative Yeast Nuclear), 13 (13 · Ascidian Mitochondrial), 14 (14 · Alternative Flatworm Mitochondrial), 15 (15 · Blepharisma Macronuclear), 16 (16 · Chlorophycean Mitochondrial), 21 (21 · Trematode Mitochondrial), 22 (22 · Scenedesmus obliquus Mitochondrial), 23 (23 · Thraustochytrium Mitochondrial), 24 (24 · Rhabdopleuridae Mitochondrial), 25 (25 · Candidate Division SR1 and Gracilibacteria), 26 (26 · Pachysolen tannophilus Nuclear), 27 (27 · Karyorelict Nuclear), 28 (28 · Condylostoma Nuclear), 29 (29 · Mesodinium Nuclear), 30 (30 · Peritrich Nuclear), 31 (31 · Blastocrithidia Nuclear), 32 (32 · Balanophoraceae Plastid), 33 (33 · Cephalodiscidae Mitochondrial).

min_codons.description: genes with no more codons than this leave the reference and the result: the G-test's χ² limit is poor for short genes. In codons.

pool_files.description: score every named record as ONE genome, for a genome split across files (one per chromosome). Off: each file is its own genome, scored against its own usage.

sequences.description: the genomes' coding sequences: wire upstream records here, or list library document names (each record of a CDS FASTA is one gene, read in frame from its first base; each file is one genome).

name: discover_codon_outliers

genes.description: every gene scored: codons, B, MILC, G, degrees of freedom, p and q

outlierCount.description: how many genes were called outliers

outliers.description: genes at q ≤ alpha, largest MILC first

result.description: the full result, with the settings that produced it

skipped.description: genes left out as too short, with their codon counts
